opt_in: Transport.launch_grid; Session selects it explicitly or via the sim-multicore backend contract

10.name: PHYSICAL_GRID_CAP
10.r1: maximum programs in a streaming grid

11.name: PHYSICAL_GRID_LAUNCH
11.a2: uint32 role/slice flags; bits 9:8 select log2(programs per physical batch), 0/1/2; other reserved bits remain refused
11.a5: per-core argument block stride in bytes

14.name: PHYSICAL_CHUNK_CAP
14.r1: maximum logical programs per accepted per-core batch (1/2/4)
14.old_image: REFUSED; no reinterpretation of legacy row-SPMD artifacts

rules: Negotiate capability before launch; never infer physical cores from role contexts.
One request dispatches the complete logical grid, with bounded hardware queues.
Each core's arguments are at a1 + physical_core_id*a5; the host populates private scratch pointers in those blocks.
All logical axes are unsigned 32-bit and the product is checked against the advertised budget.
Code is uploaded to the shell's private-code window before launch; data accesses use coherent NUCA.
The binding preserves request sequence identity through hardware completion.
An expiry diagnostic before hardware drain poisons the simulation epoch; further writes and launches are refused.
Capability does not imply compiler role-SPMD compatibility; public runtime partitioning remains a separate integration requirement.
The new simulation binding refuses unsupported legacy single-program opcodes rather than reinterpret their metadata.

Telemetry is synthesized in the dispatcher from accepted work until core completion, including memory stalls; retained after completion until the next accepted dispatcher launch. Invalid/zero-work dispatcher launches reset counters. Out-of-range telemetry indices are refused; opcode 15 remains reserved/refused.

physical-x-chunk-v1 artifacts start at global pid.x + role lane (ROLE_ID>>1 for pairs); each active lane executes once and tail lanes exit before scratch/descriptor side effects. Global num_programs is preserved. The dispatcher reserves ceil(gx/group_width)*gy*gz batches, never crosses rows, and counts logical issued/drained programs including partial tails. Legacy row-SPMD artifacts remain refused by physical dispatch.

MEM_PORTS selects independently arbitrated home subsets before serialization. Each home is bound to controller home_id modulo MEM_PORTS, so controller replies cannot collide at a non-backpressured home response interface. All controllers preserve the full source/tag and byte line address. Wrong-controller/out-of-range sources are dropped and latch protocol_fault; global dispatch stops issuing and drains accepted work, with platform recovery required if a controller lost an accepted response. Counts are synthesized from real memory handshakes; they do not establish board HBM traffic. Logical simulator capacity remains memory_bytes even when sparse controller arrays each model the global address space.
